annotatedSteps.description: Identify the type of lens from the sign of power
annotatedSteps.studentWork: Since the power is negative, X is a concave lens.

annotatedSteps.description: Calculate focal length in cm using f = 1/P
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ½ Correct formula, but 1/(-2.5) equals -0.4 m (-40 cm), not -4 m

annotatedSteps.description: Name the eye defect corrected by this lens
State nature and size of the image
annotatedSteps.studentWork: m = −2 (negative) ⇒ (I) the image is real and inverted; (II) it is twice the size of the object (magnified);
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Both nature and size correctly deduced from magnification

annotatedSteps.description: Determine image position and sign of image height
annotatedSteps.studentWork: (III) v = m × u = (−2) × (−20) = +40 cm, i.e. 40 cm on the other side of the lens, beyond 2F; (IV) the height of the image is negative.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct position and sign of height

annotatedSteps.description: Identify lens with higher convergence/divergence and provide reason
annotatedSteps.studentWork: Lens A (f = 10 cm), because power P = 1/f — the shorter the focal length, the greater the power, i.e. the higher the degree of convergence/divergence.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Lens A correctly chosen with proper reasoning

teacherNote: Marked against: (i) Identification of lens X as concave lens (0.5); (i) Calculation of focal length in cm (f = -40 cm) (1); (i) Name of defect of vision (myopia / short-sightedness) (0.5); (ii)(I) Nature of the image (real and inverted) (0.5); (ii)(II) Size of the image (magnified / twice the size of object) (0.5); (ii)(III) Position of the image (v = +40 cm / 40 cm on the opposite side) (0.5); (ii)(IV) Sign of the height of the image (negative) (0.5); (iii) Identification of Lens A (0.5); (iii) Justification relating power inversely to focal length (P = 1/f) (0.5). Very well-structured answers across all subparts with clear reasoning and correct sign conventions. Be careful with decimal division: 1/2.5 is 0.4, not 4, which led to an incorrect focal length of -400 cm instead of -40 cm.
